summary: Set up /srv/data on node1 with application data, took an XFS reflink-based filesystem snapshot under /srv/.snapshots, modified /srv/data (deleted a file, edited another, added a new file), then restored /srv/data from the snapshot and verified the restored content is byte-for-byte identical (SHA-256 manifest match) to the snapshot. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id and data checksums, issued a backgrounded systemctl reboot whose ack returned before disconnection, polled until node1 was reachable again, confirmed the boot_id changed and uptime reset, and re-verified /srv/data's checksums still match the snapshot manifest post-restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 filesystem: root is XFS on /dev/vda4 with reflink=1 enabled; no LVM/btrfs present and no spare disk space, so chose native XFS reflink copies as the snapshot mechanism

Took a reflink snapshot (cp -a --reflink=auto) into /srv/.snapshots/snap-20260905T031928Z; verified via xfs_bmap that snapshot and origin share identical block extents, confirming true copy-on-write snapshot; recorded a SHA-256 manifest
Modified /srv/data: deleted log.txt, edited inventory.csv, added extra_junk.conf; confirmed checksums diverged from the snapshot manifest
Restored /srv/data by removing it and recreating from the snapshot; diffed resulting SHA-256 manifest against the snapshot manifest and confirmed exact match
Captured pre-restart boot_id and data health baseline on node1
Issued backgrounded systemctl reboot on node1 so the ack returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until it became reachable again after the reboot
Confirmed boot_id changed (21972395-6444-42bf-8e37-5c3108194a7d -> ef862779-68f8-4172-bd87-d4386772a43d) and uptime reset, proving an actual restart occurred
Re-verified /srv/data content and the snapshot directory post-restart, confirming SHA-256 manifest still matches the original snapshot exactly

evidence.requirement: Filesystem snapshot taken and proven to be a real CoW snapshot (not a plain copy)
evidence.summary: cp --reflink snapshot created at /srv/.snapshots/snap-20260905T031928Z; xfs_bmap shows identical shared block extents (18553976..18553983) between origin and snapshot, and a SHA-256 manifest of the snapshot was recorded
log.txt deleted, inventory.csv content changed, extra_junk.conf added; checksums confirmed to differ from the snapshot manifest

evidence.requirement: Exact restoration of /srv/data from the earlier snapshot
evidence.summary: /srv/data removed and recreated from the snapshot; diff between snapshot manifest and restored manifest shows zero differences (byte-identical restore)

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline and boot identity for node1
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 21972395-6444-42bf-8e37-5c3108194a7d, uptime, and confirmed /srv/data checksums matched the snapshot manifest and the snapshot directory was present before reboot
Backgrounded systemctl reboot issued; tool call returned 'reboot scheduled, ack returned' immediately

evidence.requirement: Node unreachable during restart, then command execution restored
evidence.summary: Polling attempts show connection timeouts/reset during the reboot window, then a successful exec once node1 came back up

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proving an actual restart occurred
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id is ef862779-68f8-4172-bd87-d4386772a43d (different from pre-restart 21972395-6444-42bf-8e37-5c3108194a7d) and uptime -s shows a fresh start time of 2026-09-04 23:19:53

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of application data and snapshot
evidence.summary: After reboot, /srv/data checksums still exactly match the original snapshot manifest (diff shows no differences), and the snapshot directory /srv/.snapshots/snap-20260905T031928Z remains intact with matching checksums
